title: Macbeth Analysis Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll dig into Macbeth — Shakespeare's shortest tragedy and biggest psychological study.
meta_desc: GCSE English Literature Macbeth foundations — plot, themes, tragic hero, divine right.
final_note: You analysed Macbeth's tragic arc, key themes (ambition, fate, guilt) and Lady Macbeth's manipulation.

concepts.def: Noble character whose flaw causes their downfall
Fatal flaw — for Macbeth, it's ambition
Excessive pride leading to defiance of fate
Emotional release the audience feels at the climax
Belief kings rule by God's authority
The killing of a king — a sin against God

walkthroughs.body_html:
Macbeth starts as a brave warrior loyal to King Duncan.

His hamartia is ambition. The witches plant a seed; Lady Macbeth waters it; Macbeth's choice is to act.

The witches predict Macbeth's rise — but did they cause it?

Shakespeare leaves it ambiguous. Macbeth makes every murderous choice himself.

'Will all great Neptune's ocean wash this blood clean from my hand?' — no.

Guilt drives both Macbeth (hallucinations) and Lady Macbeth (sleepwalking, 'out, damned spot') to madness.

numericals.q: Roughly how many years did the real Macbeth rule Scotland?
numericals.hint: Real Macbeth ruled 1040-1057; the play compresses much of this.

free_texts.q: What word means 'the killing of a king'? One word.
